seoTitle: Generate Reports in Monday.com With Dashboards
metaDescription: Build a monday.com report with a dashboard: connect boards (1 to 50 depending on plan), add widgets, then share it or send it to outsiders as a scheduled PDF.
intro:
Rebuilding the same status spreadsheet every week gets old fast. In monday.com the report is a dashboard: a page that pulls live data from the boards you connect to it and shows it through widgets such as charts, battery bars, numbers and tables. Change a status on a board and the dashboard reflects it.

This guide builds one from scratch using a payment-status board as the example. It also covers two limits that shape what you can build: how many boards your plan lets one dashboard combine, and the fact that dashboards can only be opened by people with a monday.com account.
prerequisites: At least one board with the data you want to report on, including the status, number or date columns the widgets will read
View access to every board you plan to connect, and membership of the workspace each one lives in

steps.heading: Create the dashboard
steps.body:
In the left sidebar, click the + below your workspace name and choose New Dashboard. To place it inside a folder, open the folder's three-dot menu, select Create in folder, then New Dashboard.

A dashboard is its own item type. It sits in the sidebar next to your boards and holds no items of its own, only views of data that lives on boards.

image.caption: The Add new menu in the workspace sidebar, with Dashboard listed among Board, Doc, and Workflow as a distinct item type.

steps.heading: Name it and choose Main or Private
steps.body:
The Create dashboard dialog asks for a name and a type. Main is visible to everyone in your account. Private is visible only to you and the people you invite, which suits financial or HR figures.

Name it after what it reports on, like "Q3 Payments", not after who built it. Months later, in a sidebar full of boards, that is what people will scan for. A dashboard can be deleted but not archived, so there is no soft way to retire one later.

image.caption: The Create dashboard dialog, with a name field and a choice between Main (visible to everyone) and Private.

steps.heading: Connect the boards to report on
steps.body:
Open Connect boards and select the boards whose data you want. Every widget reads only from these connected boards, so if a number looks wrong later, this list is the first thing to check.

Your plan caps how many boards one dashboard can combine: 1 on Free, 5 on Standard, 20 on Pro and 50 on Enterprise. Separately, all connected boards together must stay under 20,000 items, subitems and linked items. If a board you expect is missing from the picker, you are probably not subscribed to its workspace or lack view access to it.

steps.heading: Add widgets from the Widgets Center
steps.body:
Toggle the dashboard to Edit at the top of the screen, then click Add widget to open the Widgets Center. Categories run down the left. Under Staying on Top you will find Battery for overall progress, Numbers for totals across number columns, Gauge for targets, and List View, Table and Board Updates for row-level detail. For a breakdown by status, add the Chart widget.

A dashboard holds up to 30 widgets, with Text widgets not counted. Widgets can only show columns that exist on the connected boards. If a column exists on some boards but not others, only the boards that have it feed that widget. Toggle back to View when you finish.

image.caption: The Widgets Center's Staying on Top category, showing Battery, Numbers, Gauge, List View, Table, and Board Updates widgets available to add.

steps.heading: Read and filter the result
steps.body:
In the example, a Chart widget built on the payment-status column shows counts for Paid, Not Paid and Payment pending, using the same colours as the board's labels. A Battery widget beside it rolls the same data into one completion bar for readers who do not need row detail.

To narrow the whole dashboard, click the Filter icon at the top right, pick a connected board, then choose columns and values. Quick filters cover board, group or column. Advanced filters combine conditions across several columns.

image.caption: A bar chart widget breaking down items by payment status, alongside a Battery widget showing overall completion as a percentage.

steps.heading: Share it, or send a PDF to people outside monday
steps.body:
Teammates and guests with a monday.com account can be given access to the dashboard itself, which stays live. People without an account cannot open a dashboard at all. For them, click Export at the top right and choose Export to PDF, which captures every widget in its current state.

For a recurring report, choose Schedule PDF export from the same Export button. You set recipients (up to 50), a subject and message, a daily, weekly or monthly schedule, and portrait or landscape layout. Two widgets, Table and Timeline, can also go to Excel from their own three-dot menus. A whole dashboard cannot be exported to Excel.

tables.title: Dashboard limits by monday.com plan
tables.note: From monday.com's support articles, September 2026. The scheduled figure is how many schedules you can set up, not how many times they send. Scheduled email notifications of a dashboard are Enterprise-only.

troubleshooting.problem: A board does not appear in the Connect boards picker
troubleshooting.cause: You are not subscribed to the workspace that contains it, or you do not have view access to the board.
troubleshooting.fix: Join the workspace, or ask the board owner to share the board with you, then reopen the picker.

troubleshooting.problem: A warning says the dashboard is over its limit
troubleshooting.cause: The connected boards together exceed 20,000 items, subitems and linked items.
troubleshooting.fix: Disconnect boards you no longer need or the ones contributing the most items, and use filters instead of connecting more boards.

troubleshooting.problem: A column you need is missing from a widget
troubleshooting.cause: Widgets only read columns that exist on the connected boards. Mirror columns show empty if the mirror is not populated on the board.
troubleshooting.fix: Add the column to the board (or fix the mirror), and check that every board meant to feed the widget has it.

faq.question: What's the difference between a board and a dashboard?
faq.answer: A board holds the work items and their data. A dashboard holds no items; it connects to boards and displays their data through widgets.

faq.question: How many boards can one dashboard combine?
faq.answer: It depends on the plan: 1 on Free, 5 on Standard, 20 on Pro and 50 on Enterprise, with a combined ceiling of 20,000 items.

faq.question: Can I share a dashboard with a client who doesn't use monday.com?
faq.answer: Not as a live dashboard. Only people with a monday.com account can open it. Send an exported or scheduled PDF instead.

faq.question: Can I export a dashboard to Excel?
faq.answer: Not as a whole. The Table and Timeline widgets export to Excel individually, and the Chart widget exports as a file of its own. The full dashboard exports to PDF.

faq.question: Can a dashboard show data straight from Excel?
faq.answer: No. Dashboards only read monday.com boards. Import the data or sync it into a board first.
